prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: C01-ARCH-TWIN-HILLS, the Twin Hills battlefield LOCATION plate in The Oath of the Broken Crown, an opaque architectural/landscape catalog scene.
Create ONE finished landscape image at 1672 x 941 if available, approximately 16:9, safe for a centered exact 1664 x 936 crop. Edge-to-edge opaque painting, no panels or borders.
Input roles: Image 1 is the original exact Twin Hills source cell, CONTENT AND GEOGRAPHIC LOGIC reference. Images 2 and 3 are approved narrative STYLE references only. Do not copy tents, people or hospital equipment from those style references. Rebuild the original terrain with the clearer chunky style and a deliberately wide landscape composition.
Subject and scene: an unoccupied rugged border battlefield landscape, two principal rock-and-grass hill masses facing one another across a narrow meandering blue-gray stream gorge. Each hill has stepped broad grassy/dirt terraces, flat summit clearings bordered by sparse short rough wooden stakes and rails, paths connecting the different elevations, and a few short timber stairs. Two simple rough plank footbridges cross the stream at different depths: one near the center middle distance, one farther downstream in the lower foreground. This paired-hill / intervening-stream / two-crossings logic is the identity, not any village or army arrangement. A small upstream cascade, big slate-gray rock faces, restrained mossy turf and pine woods at the outer edges complete the same place. Preserve the source's empty prepared clearings, broad tan paths and physical navigability. No strategic labels or invented direction markers.
Composition: elevated three-quarter wide environmental view, looking along the stream between the two hill masses. Both main hill shoulders and their flat upper clearings must be visible together at 256 x 144. Make the full paired terrain dominate the landscape, with clear readable separations of upper ground, lower routes, stream and bridge decks. Let the winding stream and both modest crossings stay near the central region, while the hill terraces spread to each side. Do not crop the upper hill clearings against the top edge. This is a location establishing plate, not an isometric gameplay grid or a single reusable terrain tile.
Style: match approved camp and hospital images: strong stable dark contours, broad chunky matte hand-painted fantasy forms, large clean cel-shaded planes, simple grouped stone facets and tree silhouettes. Restrained detail with plenty of quiet shape interiors. Rocks are broad slabs, not hundreds of little pebbles. Dirt paths are smooth ochre shapes with sparse large stones, not stippled gravel. Grassy platforms use broad olive-green planes, not individual grass blades. Water uses a few large flat blue bands and simple white accents, not noisy reflections. Muted warm earth, moss green, slate gray and cool blue water under soft daylight; readable values, clear silhouettes.
Constraints: no people, soldiers, commanders, named heroes, flags, military emblems, arrows, tactical deployment, fortresses, villages, ruins, memorial monuments, battles, corpses, dramatic fire or story action. Do not assert which pictured side is north or assign forces to a hill. No year-four monument state. Do not reproduce the old board's noisy microtexture, miniature repeated-cell tiling or panel border. No words, numbers, labels, logo or watermark. Fully opaque.
